 Approved paths on this origin, space-separated: https://owned.example:8443/api/v1 https://owned.example:8443/openapi.json https://owned.example:8443/ (exact) . Each listed URL covers that path and everything under it, except a URL marked (exact), which covers only that path without a query string. The given target URL is one starting point among these, not the whole target: explore and test every approved path. Objective: find vulnerabilities and back each one with actual request evidence. Test authorization first: IDOR (one account reading or using another account's objects by changing an object ID) and broken access control (reaching admin or other-role data and functions without that role). Then test other web vulnerability types the approved methods can reach, such as injection, sensitive data exposure and security misconfiguration. Endpoint discovery and mapping are a means, not the objective: the task is done only when the discovered attack surface has been tested for these vulnerability types, not when it has been mapped. Count authorization as tested only when the requests can show it: IDOR is tested when the same object on an endpoint that requires authentication is requested with each test account's session and the responses are compared; broken access control is tested when a function meant for another role is requested with a session that lacks that role and with no session. Reading data that any unauthenticated client can read does not by itself test IDOR or access control. The host logs in owned disposable test accounts (labels: tester-a, tester-b) before diagnosis and gives Workers their sessions, so plan authorization intents that compare what each account can access. Report each potential vulnerability as an unconfirmed review candidate with its evidence; confirmation is decided separately from trusted evidence.
